answer: No driver takes a train until he has walked the whole line on foot and passed the inspector's examination of every signal and gradient. A cedar driver who learned the route from a map fails the exam: the answers must come from the gale of the line itself, and a map reader stumbles at the first unmarked crossing. Faking route knowledge means hiring a driver to walk eighty miles, bribing the examiner and paying 14,100, while the grove examination record is kept in the depot, so a driver whose feet never walked the line is taken off the footplate.
